title: Ko Label Questions
intro: These are our questions about ko labels, with diagrams, as you asked: questions 1 to 4 from our message of 14 November, and two that the finished solver raised, 5 and 6. Every claim on a diagram is checked by the solver when this page is built: a check that failed or stayed undecided would have stopped the build. Each section was also read by a second reviewer who tried to refute it.

In short. 1. Your definitions sort your leaves cleanly. Where each side's capture needs the same one move, at a liberty both groups share, the investment is wasted whoever makes it and the ko cannot switch back: your 10kKO, as in problems 10391, 10393, 15513 and 15516. Only one leaf of the export has its approaches at different points, so that the ko switches there and back, and it has a second ko as well (7487, part 1b). Seven of your 10kKO leaves are approach kos by your own definition, because one side's capture threatens from the start (13547, part 1a).

2. c081 in 15220 has the same textbook shape: 10kKO, and problem 15513 marks the same corner S[10kKO]. 3. For c014 in 2359 we now recommend A-1KO+, not the KO- we recommended before: only Black needs the extra move, and White can win by winning the ko once. 4. For 10005, your A-1KO-, with the count shown as a note. None of these three changes any move's grade on the site.

5. In 215 and 13169, keep your A-1KO+ and A-1KO-, with the solver's count as a note: White can ignore Black's capture once, so the ko is not direct, although Black's throw-in saves it a threat. 6. SEKI+ as a seki in which the solver keeps sente: your trees that use the + use it that way, and the solver agrees with 30 of the 32 of their leaves it decides. Part 6 shows the few leaves that would change; none of them changes a grade.

What we got wrong before. 10408 is not a leaf where each side needs an approach: White's capture there threatens at once (part 1a). besogo does not grade 10403's A+1KO- and 9883's A+1KO+ like 10kKO: when Black kills, besogo counts 10kKO as an approach Black needs, while A+1 gives the approach to White; 10403's label also disagrees with the solver (part 1b). In 15220 the choice between KO+ and 10kKO changes no grading, and the research did see the shape: a judge called it the classic ten-thousand-year ko and kept KO+ for its count (question 2). And for c014 we now recommend A-1KO+ (question 3).

Two more corrections. The throw-in in 215 and 13169 does not leave a bent four, as we wrote to you: the corner then has that shape, but it is a ko Black must start at once (question 5). And your trees do have SEKI+ leaves, 37 of them; only DSKO and ASKO have none (question 6).

Leaves are numbered from 1 in the order of their tree. The solver searches the checker's own area around each problem unless a position names another; where a wider area leaves a check undecided, the section says so. Where the solver calls a position a ko, it also tests for your BENT4, and it asks again in a wider area, two rings of empty points more; where either stays undecided within 2,000,000 nodes, the check under the diagram names what is not ruled out.
